questions.question: What is the function of cytochrome P450?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Detoxification of xenobiotics**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytochrome P450 enzymes** play a crucial role in the **detoxification of xenobiotics**, which include drugs, pollutants, and other foreign substances.
 
• These enzymes are primarily found in the liver and are involved in the metabolism and elimination of various compounds from the body.
 
• The detoxification process often involves oxidation, which makes the xenobiotics more water-soluble and easier to excrete.
 
• In addition to detoxification, cytochrome P450 enzymes are also involved in the metabolism of endogenous substrates such as steroids and fatty acids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The cytochrome P450 superfamily includes a large number of enzymes that are classified based on their sequence similarities.
 
• These enzymes are named with the prefix "CYP" followed by a number indicating the gene family, a letter indicating the subfamily, and another number indicating the individual gene (e.g., CYP3A4).
 
• Inhibition or induction of cytochrome P450 enzymes can lead to significant drug interactions, affecting the efficacy and toxicity of medications.
 
• Understanding the function and regulation of cytochrome P450 enzymes is crucial for the development of new drugs and for predicting drug interactions.

questions.question: Stupas are a symbol of which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhism**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Stupas are a symbol of **Buddhism**.
 
• They are mound-like or hemispherical structures containing relics (typically the remains of Buddhist monks or nuns) and are used as a place of meditation.
 
• The stupa serves as a significant form of Buddhist architecture and is considered a sacred structure in Buddhism.
 
• Famous stupas include the Sanchi Stupa in India, the Shwedagon Pagoda in Myanmar, and the Borobudur Stupa in Indonesia.
 
• Stupas are often decorated with carvings and statues that depict various aspects of Buddhist teachings and history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhism** was founded by Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha, in the 5th century BCE in ancient India.
 
• The core teachings of Buddhism include the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path, which guide individuals towards enlightenment.
 
• Buddhism emphasizes the importance of meditation, ethical conduct, and wisdom in achieving spiritual goals.
 
• There are several branches of Buddhism, including Theravada, Mahayana, and Vajrayana, each with its own unique practices and interpretations of the Buddha's teachings.
 
• Buddhism has a significant cultural and historical impact on many countries in Asia and has also spread to other parts of the world.

questions.question: As per the Indian Constitution, the size of the Council of Ministers shall NOT exceed:

options.text: 15 percent of total number of members of the House of the People
25 percent of total number of members of the House of the People
10 percent of total number of members of the House of the People
20 percent of total number of members of the House of the People

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 percent of total number of members of the House of the People**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The size of the Council of Ministers** in India shall NOT exceed **15 percent** of the total number of members of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• This provision is outlined in the **91st Amendment Act** of 2003.
 
• The amendment was introduced to limit the size of the Council of Ministers to ensure better governance and to prevent excessive expenditure.
 
• The **House of the People (Lok Sabha)** currently has 543 members, so the maximum number of ministers can be 81 (15% of 543).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **91st Amendment Act** also made it mandatory for a member of the legislature to be disqualified from being a minister if they are disqualified under the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law).
 
• The **Indian Constitution** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts provided the title of the Viceroy to the Governor-General of India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1858** provided the title of Viceroy to the Governor-General of India.
 
• This act marked the end of the rule of the East India Company and the beginning of direct control by the British Crown over India.
 
• The Viceroy was the representative of the British Crown in India and had extensive administrative powers.
 
• This change was a result of the Indian Rebellion of 1857, which led to significant reorganization of the administrative structure in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** was a significant step towards centralization and gave the Governor-General more power but did not provide the title of Viceroy.
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first step towards regulating the affairs of the East India Company but did not introduce the title of Viceroy.
 
• The **Charter Act of 1853** was an important legislative act but it did not provide the title of Viceroy either.
 
• The title of Viceroy was specifically introduced to indicate the representative role of the British Crown in India, which was a significant shift in the administrative framework.

• During the festival, large tree trunks are brought from the forest and are immersed in a sacred pool called 'Wah-ei-lad'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meghalaya** is known for its rich cultural heritage and diverse tribal communities.
 
• The state is also famous for its scenic beauty, with numerous waterfalls, caves, and lush green landscapes.
 
• The capital city of Meghalaya is **Shillong**, which is often referred to as the 'Scotland of the East' due to its picturesque landscapes.
 
• Apart from Behdienkhlam, other major festivals celebrated in Meghalaya include **Wangala, Nongkrem Dance, and Shad Suk Mynsiem.**
 
• Meghalaya became a full-fledged state on **21st January 1972**, after being carved out from Assam.

questions.question: The thermocline layer is the _______ layer of the ocean.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**second**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **thermocline layer** is the **second** layer of the ocean.
 
• The thermocline is characterized by a rapid change in temperature with depth.
 
• It lies between the mixed layer at the surface and the deep water layer.
 
• This layer acts as a barrier to the mixing of surface water and deep water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **mixed layer** is the topmost layer of the ocean and is well-mixed due to wind and waves.
 
• Below the thermocline is the **deep water layer**, where the temperature decreases more gradually with depth.
 
• The thermocline plays a crucial role in ocean dynamics and marine life distribution.
 
• Understanding the thermocline is important for climate studies, as it affects heat distribution and ocean circulation.
